beats.narration_en: How do you stop a truck that's lost its brakes?
On some steep mountain roads, you catch it in a giant net.
Steel cable nets hang across the ramp, one after another.
Each one is tied to steel tape, coiled up in boxes inside the walls.
When the truck hits, the tape is dragged through pins that bend it back and forth.
Bending all that steel soaks up the speed, net after net.
The catch is gentle enough to protect the driver.
They're built to stop a ninety-thousand-pound truck at ninety miles an hour.
Then crews swap in fresh tape, and it's ready again in about four hours.
